eda_descriptions.01_correlation_heatmap.png: Attendance Rate (r=0.73) and quiz2 score (r=0.68) are the strongest single predictors of total score. Attendance and assignment score correlate more weakly on their own — the takeaway is that quiz performance is the most reliable early signal of a student's likely outcome.
eda_descriptions.02_top_features_scatter.png: 'Good' students cluster toward the top-right, averaging 93.9 on Attendance Rate and 13.8 on quiz2 score, while 'fail' students cluster toward the bottom-left, averaging only 78.9 and 10.4 respectively. The two groups are visibly separable using just these two scores — confirming they carry most of the signal needed to flag at-risk students early.
eda_descriptions.03_feature_distributions.png: Attendance ranges from 52% to 100% (average 85%), and both quiz and assignment scores are spread across their full possible range with no extreme outliers — the data doesn't need outlier removal or capping before it's used to train the models.
eda_descriptions.04_total_score_distribution.png: Total scores span 25 to 100 out of 100, centered around 65. The spread is wide enough that a single model has real work to do separating strong and weak students, rather than everyone landing in a narrow band.
eda_descriptions.05_class_imbalance.png: 'Average' is the dominant outcome at 1168 students (58.4%), while 'poor' is rare at just 25 students (1.2%). In practice, this means the predictor will be most confident calling out 'average' and 'fail' cases, and should be double-checked by a human advisor whenever it flags the less common 'poor' or 'good' categories.
eda_descriptions.06_feature_relationships.png: All four features trend upward with total score — none of them work against the others. Attendance Rate shows the steepest, most consistent climb, reinforcing that it's the single most actionable lever: improving it is the most direct way for a student to raise their predicted score.
eda_descriptions.07_boxplots_by_class.png: Median attendance rises step by step from 79% for 'fail' students to 95% for 'good' students, with almost no overlap between the extremes. Attendance alone is a dependable early-warning signal, well before quiz or assignment results come in.
eda_descriptions.08_pairplot.png: The four input features correlate with each other only weakly (strongest pairwise correlation: 0.56), meaning each one adds genuinely new information rather than repeating what another feature already shows — there's no redundant data being collected here.
eda_descriptions.09_missing_values.png: The raw dataset arrived with 0 missing values across 7 columns and 2000 rows. No imputation or row-dropping was needed before training — the data was clean going in.
